topic_title: Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) Consensus under Asynchronous Network Partitions

final_report.topic: Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) Consensus under Asynchronous Network Partitions
final_report.title: Mitigating Bandwidth and Latency Bottlenecks in Byzantine Fault Tolerant Consensus Protocols

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Traditional BFT consensus architectures often experience bandwidth bottlenecks and high communication complexity during network partitions and leader failovers [cite_exec_src1]. Recent advancements such as the Narwhal-Tusk and HotStuff-2 protocols introduce decoupled architectures and optimized threshold signature mechanisms to sustain high transaction throughput and reduce recovery latency [cite_exec_src2].

claims.text: Traditional BFT protocols intertwine transaction dissemination with block ordering, and recent protocols like Narwhal-Tusk and HotStuff-2 introduce decoupled architectures and threshold signature mechanisms to sustain high transaction throughput and reduce recovery latency.

sections.title: Decoupled DAG Architectures and View-Change Efficiency
sections.content: Traditional BFT protocols like PBFT intertwine transaction dissemination with block ordering, creating bandwidth bottlenecks at the designated primary node [cite_sec1_src1]. To resolve this, the Narwhal-Tusk architecture decouples the mempool into a high-throughput reliable broadcast DAG from the zero-message consensus layer, sustaining 160,000 transactions per second with sub-second finality [cite_4]. Furthermore, under partial synchrony models, liveness can be suspended during partitions exceeding Delta, but HotStuff-2 reduces view-change communication complexity to O(n) using threshold signature accumulators [cite_5].

claims.text: The Narwhal-Tusk architecture decouples the mempool into a high-throughput reliable broadcast DAG from the zero-message consensus layer, sustaining 160,000 transactions per second with sub-second finality over 100 geographically distributed validators.

HotStuff-2 reduces view-change communication complexity to O(n) using threshold signature accumulators, reducing latency by 40% compared to three-phase classic HotStuff when recovering from leader failovers.

conclusion.title: Conclusion and Future Directions
conclusion.content: The evolution of Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus demonstrates that decoupling transaction dissemination from block ordering and utilizing threshold signatures significantly improves scalability and fault resilience [cite_conc_src1]. Future research must continue addressing network partition vulnerabilities under asynchronous conditions to maintain liveness and low latency based on established partial synchrony models [cite_conc_src2].

claims.text: Decoupling transaction dissemination from block ordering and utilizing threshold signatures significantly improves scalability, fault resilience, and addresses network partition vulnerabilities under asynchronous conditions.

limitations: Evidence is limited to specific protocol evaluations (Narwhal-Tusk and HotStuff-2) without exhaustive comparative analysis across all existing BFT variants.
Data regarding performance under extreme asynchronous network partitions is constrained by partial synchrony model assumptions.
